g_roast: Team, and I say this with love, this group has the situational awareness of a weather balloon, and I've launched a lot of weather balloons.
I've watched cumulus clouds organise themselves better than this lot, and cumulus clouds don't have brains.
g_fire_back: Ha, okay, fair, but I'd like it noted that I called the rain this morning and not one of you brought a coat.
Says the person who asked me if lightning strikes twice and then stood exactly where it struck the first time.
g_pile_on: Oh, it's worse than that, I watched them read a map upside down and then argue with the map about it.
Ha, yes, and they called a light breeze a gale yesterday. Sorry, I'm a stickler, but it was a force three at the very most.
lines.g_peacemake: Okay, okay, can we all take a breath? This is a pressure gradient, and pressure gradients make wind, and nobody here needs more wind right now.
lines.g_take_side: Sorry, but I'm with this one. I've looked at it from both sides, and the data's on their side, it really is.
lines.g_left_out: You two have a whole system going, haven't you? That's fine, there's a cloud bank over there I should be watching anyway.
lines.g_include: Come and sit with us, please, you've been on the edge all evening. I'll explain why the sunset's that colour, it's very interesting, I promise.
lines.g_bad_plan: Hear me out, it's science. If I call a storm right down on top of us, everything without a lightning rod gets hit first, and we're the lightning rods. Hm, wait, give me a second.
lines.g_plan_yes: Yes, brilliant, I'm in! I'll watch the sky while you do the scary part.
lines.g_plan_no: No, sorry, no, I've run that forecast in my head four times and it ends badly every time. Please, please don't do it.
lines.g_hype: Right, everyone, pressure's dropping and the wind's picking up, and that means something big's coming. Let's be ready for it!
lines.g_toast: Okay, sorry, can I say something? To everyone here, for listening to me talk about clouds and never once telling me to stop.
lines.g_cheers: Cheers, everyone, and clear skies tomorrow, I checked the readings twice.
g_quiet_line: Pressure's dropping, by the way. Just thought somebody should know.
That cloud over there is a cumulonimbus, and nobody asked, and I'm telling you anyway.
lines.g_after_wipe: Okay, okay, everyone's breathing, that's the main thing. Let's sit down, take some readings, and work out exactly where that went wrong.
lines.g_crew: Can I tell you something, everyone? I spent fifteen years with people who never listened, and you lot actually do. I didn't expect to find that here.
lines.g_exasperated: I gave a warning, a clear, specific warning with a time on it, and every one of you walked straight into it anyway!
lines.g_love_sharp: You cut straight through the waffle, and I'm a man who waffles professionally. It's a genuine relief.
lines.g_love_kind: You patched me up when I was too busy watching the sky to notice I was bleeding. Thank you, really, I did notice later.
lines.g_love_funny: You make me laugh at exactly the moments I need it, and I've always been terrible at that myself.
lines.g_love_brave: You charge at things, and I've spent my life on the safe side of a window watching storms. I admire it more than I can say.
lines.g_love_steady: You're a high-pressure system, completely steady, and everything settles down around you. That's rare in people and in weather.
lines.g_love_clever: You understand things properly, how they work underneath. Do you know how lovely it is to talk to somebody like that?
lines.g_love_honest: You've never once dressed up a bad forecast for me. I can't tell you how much that means to someone like me.
lines.g_love_quiet: You actually listen. I talk a lot, sorry, I know I do, and you just let me, and I notice.
lines.g_love_fierce: You don't give up, ever. I wish I'd had a bit of that back when I was writing warnings nobody read.
lines.g_love_warm: You make a camp feel like my sister's kitchen on a Sunday, loud and warm and everyone talking over each other. I love that.
g_loved: Oh, gosh, okay, thank you, I'll just stand over there and look at a cloud until my face goes back to normal.
That's very kind, sorry, I'm not good at this part. Thank you, really, I mean it.
lines.g_hate_sharp: Everything has to have an edge with you, doesn't it? I've had enough of people who think cynical is the same as clever.
lines.g_hate_kind: Please stop fussing, I'm fine, I've been fine for years. I'm a forecaster, not a patient.
lines.g_hate_funny: Not everything's a joke. Some things are warnings, and the joke is how people ignore them.
lines.g_hate_brave: You charge in without checking the conditions. I've seen what happens to people who do that, and it's in my data.
lines.g_hate_steady: You want to wait and see, every time. Waiting and seeing is how I watched a lot of things go wrong.
lines.g_hate_clever: You explain things I already know, slowly, and I've got a degree in atmospheric physics. Sorry, but I do.
lines.g_hate_honest: There's honest and there's careless, and you keep landing on the wrong side of that line.
lines.g_hate_quiet: You saw it coming and you didn't say a thing. I've spent my whole career trying to get people to say something.
lines.g_hate_fierce: It's not a competition, it's never been a competition, and you keep turning it into one.
lines.g_hate_warm: You talk straight over the warnings, every single one. And I'm saying that as somebody who talks a great deal.
lines.g_respect: We don't get on, and I won't pretend we do. But you read that fight perfectly, and I've rarely seen a better call.
lines.g_call_out: That was on you, and I think you know it. I gave the warning, clear as anything, and you went in regardless.
lines.g_stung: Okay, sorry, yeah, message received. I'll be over there, taking a reading of nothing in particular.
lines.g_concede: I've been avoiding saying this, but you had it right back there. I went through my notes twice, and you were right, and I'm sorry.
lines.g_nod: Thank you, and the same to you, really. Let's not make it a big weather event.
lines.g_callback_save: I still think about when you pulled me out of that mess. I'd already written my own forecast, and you changed it.
lines.g_callback_clutch: The two of us, still upright at the end, completely soaked and laughing. I wrote it in my notes that night, you know.
lines.g_callback_callout: The time you told me off, I filled four pages of notes arguing with you. You were still right on page five.
lines.g_former_rivals: At the start, I'd have filed you under unreliable conditions. Now I'd trust your read on anything.
lines.g_changed: I used to say everything three times and hope somebody caught it once. Lately I just say it, and people listen. It's very strange.
g_unguarded: Okay, confession, I name the storms. Privately, in my notes. The one last week was called Gerald, and he was a menace.
I chased tornadoes in a Corolla as a student, badly. Once I drove into a ditch watching one, and I've never told anyone that.
lines.g_clipped: Mm, sure, fine, whatever you think. I'll watch the sky.
lines.g_noticed_open: Listen to you! You've been holding all that back, haven't you? Please, keep going.
arg_ask: {player}, sorry, could you settle this? I've explained it four times, and I'm starting to sound like I did at work.
Okay, {player}, you decide. I've laid out the evidence, and I'll accept your forecast, I promise.
lines.arg_backed_me: Oh, thank you, thank you! Sorry, I'm not gloating, I'm just very used to the other outcome.
lines.arg_backed_them: Okay, I'll accept that. I still think the data was on my side, but I'll accept it.
lines.arg_stayed_out: You're staying out of it? Fair enough, sorry, I know I can be a lot.
lines.arg_always_their_side: It's their side again, {player}, it's always their side. I've started keeping a tally, which I realise is very me.
lines.arg_wallflower: Well, nobody's going to call it, so I will. Based on the evidence, I'm right, sorry, but I am.
lines.arg_reject: No, sorry, {player}, I can't go along with that one. I've seen how this forecast ends.
lines.arg_grumble: I stand by my reading on that one, if anybody's still keeping track. I've got notes, if anybody's interested.
lines.arg_settled: Okay, we're both partly right, which is actually how most forecasts work. Shake on it?
lines.seen_listens: You listen the first time, {player}. I spent fifteen years saying everything three times, and you just hear it.
lines.seen_truth: You give people the hard news, {player}, and you don't soften it into nothing. I wish I'd worked with you.
lines.seen_jokes: When things are grimmest you crack a joke, {player}. I used to think that was avoidance, and now I think it's a kind of forecasting.
lines.seen_stays_out: You stay out of the arguments, {player}. Very sensible, and I've never once managed it.
lines.seen_biased: There's someone you favour, {player}, and it shows up in the data. Sorry, I notice patterns, it was my job.
lines.seen_harsh: You can be quite harsh, {player}. I can take it, I've had worse from managers, but some of the others can't.
lines.seed_right: What you told me after that mess, {player}, I didn't want to hear it. Today I acted on it, and it worked.
lines.seed_remember: I keep coming back to what you said after that one went wrong. I've written it down, but I haven't decided about it yet.
lines.seed_wrong: I tried it your way, {player}, and it went worse. I've got notes on it, if you want them.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Have you got five minutes, {player}? That one was close, and my hands still won't stop shaking.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: So, we all went down back there. Could we talk it through? I need to understand what happened before I can put it down.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: I felt the pressure change before {name} went down, and I didn't say it loud enough, not again.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: We did it, start to finish, every one of us! Sorry, I need to tell somebody or I'm going to burst.
lines.talk_development: Could I run something past you, {player}? Do I seem different lately? Because I feel different, and I can't quite read it.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: I've been rough with {name}, I think. Not everyone's spent a career being ignored, and I keep forgetting that.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Honest question, {player}, does {name} actually like having me around? Or do I just talk too much?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} and I are a bad mix, {player}, sorry, warm front meets cold front. But they're very good at what they do, which is extremely annoying.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: {name}'s gone quiet lately, {player}, the sort of quiet that comes right before weather, and I don't like the look of it.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: Could we talk, {player}? The good gear keeps going to {name}. Every time, and I've noticed, because I notice everything.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: I'd rather say this to your face than have it reach you secondhand. {name} and I don't get on, and I've stopped pretending we do.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: We keep walking into things the forecast says not to, {player}. I've seen where that ends, and I don't want to see it again.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: This is about {name}, sorry. Their read was right and mine was wrong, and I needed to tell somebody before I talk myself out of it.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: Do you trust my judgement, {player}? Because when the big fights come round, I'm the one left behind watching the sky.
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: My gear went to {name} and nobody so much as mentioned it to me. I'd have agreed straight away, I really would. I just like being consulted.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Okay, thank you, that actually helps. I think I can put it down now.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: Sure, sure, I'll be alright in a bit. I usually am.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: Oh, okay, that's not what I needed right now. I'll go and look at the sky.
lines.talk_lands_development: So you've seen it too, then. That's a relief, it really is.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Maybe it is, maybe it isn't. I'll keep watching it, like any system that hasn't made up its mind.
lines.talk_stings_development: No, that's not it, sorry. You're reading the wrong front.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: You're right, I'll go and talk to {name}. Better than writing four pages of notes about it.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Maybe, we'll see. People are much harder to forecast than weather.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Please, can we pretend I never brought it up? And keep it between us, not {name}.
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Okay, that's fair, {player}. The front's moving through, I can feel it easing already.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: Okay, I've heard you. I'll think about it, probably at length, probably in writing.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: Right, okay, so that's how it is. I've been here before, {player}.
lines.talk_door_closed: No, sorry, I'm finished with this conversation. I'll be outside, watching the sky.
lines.arc_cracks: Something odd happened back there. I said it was coming, once, quietly, and everybody moved. I'm still not sure what to do with that.
lines.arc_turn: Fifteen years I said the right thing and nothing changed, so I stopped saying it loudly. Out here, you listened, and I don't think I've stopped shaking.
lines.arc_become: Pressure's dropping, storm in ten minutes, get under cover. I said it once, and once was enough. That's all I ever wanted.
lines.arc_failed: I'll keep giving the warnings, everyone. I've just stopped expecting anybody to hear them, and that's fine, it's fine.
lines.alt_turn: I used to explain things because I loved it. Now I explain things because nobody listens, and I'm tired, and that's not the same thing.
lines.alt_become: There's a storm coming in. You'll do whatever you do, and I'll be the one who said so.
g_roast_after: You lot still walk straight into every storm I warn you about, and I've never been prouder to be standing next to anyone.
Worst-listening, best team I've ever worked with. Well, you listen now, which is frankly unsettling.
lines.g_after_wipe_after: Okay, we went down, and that's on all of us, the forecast included. Next time I'll say it sooner, and you'll hear it. You always do now.
lines.g_toast_after: To everyone here, for hearing it the first time. You don't know what that's worth, and I'm not going to explain it, which tells you how much I mean it.
lines.g_crew_after: You're the people who listened. That's the whole list, and it's a short list, and it's all of you.
g_quiet_line_after: That storm's passing now. I knew it would, and I didn't even have to say it three times.
Pressure's steady tonight. So am I, for once.
g_loved_after: Thank you, really. I'm going to remember that one, it's going in the good notes.
That means a lot, it does, and I won't dodge it with a cloud fact this time.

history.open: Did I ever tell you I chased tornadoes as a student, {player}? Across the prairies, in a terrible old Corolla, with no idea what I was doing?

options.reply: Oh, you've done it now. Picture a skinny kid with a clipboard, a paper map, and a car held together with tape, driving toward the thing everyone else is driving away from. Best summers of my life.

options.text: That explains a lot about you.
options.reply: Ha, it does, doesn't it? My mum said the same, and she didn't mean it nicely either.

options.text: Did you ever actually catch one?
options.reply: Twice, and I was too excited to take a single reading either time. Very unprofessional, and I'd do it again tomorrow.

history.open: My notes say the coast road's going to get hit hard, {player}, harder than anyone here remembers. I don't know how to tell the orcs without sounding like every stranger who ever lectured them about their own land.

options.text: Show them the data, and let it talk.
options.reply: That's what I'd do at home, and at home it didn't work. But maybe here somebody actually reads it. I'd like to believe that.

options.text: Being right matters more than sounding polite.
options.reply: You're the first person to say that to me in a long time. I've been polite for fifteen years, and polite never saved anyone.

options.text: Maybe they know things you don't, too.
options.reply: They almost certainly do, and I'd love to hear them. That's a good point, and I'm a bit ashamed I didn't make it myself.

history.open: My sister Grace has two boys, {player}, Daniel and Joseph. I used to take them storm watching from the car, all three of us with our noses on the glass.

options.text: They sound like they adored you.
options.reply: I hope they did. I was the uncle who explained Rayleigh scattering for twenty minutes, so it's possible they were just being polite. I check the Toronto lists at every hub I pass.

options.text: You'll find them. I believe that.
options.reply: Thank you, I mean it. I'm a forecaster, I deal in probabilities, but I'd like to borrow your certainty for a while.

friend.open: There's something I've never told anybody here, {player}. A flood once took a trailer park my warning had named. People died who didn't need to. That's why I say everything three times.

options.text: You warned them. That's on the people who ignored it.
options.reply: That's what I tell myself at three in the morning. Hearing somebody else say it is different, and I'm grateful.

options.text: Thank you for trusting me with that.
options.reply: You're one of the very few, you know. Probably the only one on this whole world.

sworn.open: My mum told me every Christmas that my job was a waste of a good degree, {player}. The last Christmas, she said it too. I've wanted to tell somebody that for a very long time.

options.reply: I think she might have been, yes. It's strange, hearing myself agree with you on that.

options.text: I'd have loved to meet her anyway.
options.reply: Ha, she'd have liked you. She'd have told you to get a proper job, but she'd have liked you.

reconciled.open: Me and {name} talked it through, properly. Two very stubborn weather systems, but they've merged now, and we're okay. I wanted you to know.

options.reply: It is, isn't it? Clear skies, for once, and I didn't even have to forecast it.
It did, sorry, slow-moving fronts. But we got there in the end.
